Affine interpolation of the two nonnegative half-width profiles produces an actual compact convex body with all five exact integer fibers. Concavity follows from the six displayed second differences, independently recomputed from the contracted widths. Each is negative for 0≤epsilon<1/7, with the y difference at base -1 reaching zero only at the excluded right endpoint.

The original areas are 4,35/2,24,35/2,4, totaling 67. Central reflection gives exact half mass for any nonvertical through-origin cap and at least half for a vertical one. For any mark a nonzero cylindrical functional nonnegative there supplies a containing cap no larger than its through-origin cap, proving the old global maximum.

Each rectangle face has one quarter of the cone mass by equal-area cones and its law is uniform along the face. Using one boundary-square variable and the specified coordinate maps produces both required relation marginals and targets (5Z_x/2,7Z_y/4) and (2Z_x,3Z_y/2). The selected cap planes intersect the relevant source and target faces only in finitely many points, or miss them entirely in strict full or empty cases, so the cone nullity holds.

Recomputed the complete six-bit target signature law by exact rational partitioning of the four faces. All individual probabilities are 1/2, each directed crossing for the first two rows is 1/160, and the third pair agrees. The two diagrams have the same target events pointwise because the tilt vanishes at base zero. The budget values a=b=35 and c=8 then give fixed credit 35/2 and adaptive credits 351/20,351/20,35/2.

The raw normal balance is (1,1,2). The raw coareas for the cylindrical cuts are (15,15,20), from twice each smaller half-width on the diagonals and twice each horizontal half-width for -y. Passing to unit normals multiplies both the balance coefficient and the raw coarea by the same norm per row. Thus their ratios give (2/7,2/7,3/7) and the weighted adaptive credit 1227/70. Each cylindrical cap captures precisely half of each centered rectangle and each shell, hence its exact loss derivative is 39 and its zero-threshold normalized common mass is identically 1/2.

At every nonzero base the absolute continuous margin is at most the sum of the rectangle half-widths, strictly less than 10|z|. The tilt is therefore strictly full on positive bases and strictly empty on negative bases, a classification preserved by nested contraction. Only the center has proper coareas (4,4,6). Exact rational evaluation gives (3/10,3/10,2/5), weighted lower credit 1753/100<39, and actual derivative 43 because only selected positive bases 1 and 2 contribute. Their common mass is 67/2-(43/2)tau=M_epsilon/2-2tau.

For base 1, the two explicit margins ±x+10(z-1) cover its whole plane and miss all lower bases while capturing base 2. Their masses are bounded by 35/4+4=51/4. The corresponding reverse tilt handles base -1 and the outward endpoint pairs each have mass at most 2. Contraction leaves these covers and mass bounds valid. Direct rational comparison at tau=13/49 shows even the lower endpoint bound 67/2-(43/2)(13/49) exceeds 51/4. The balanced tilted caps cover the middle plane and have mass strictly below M_epsilon/2 for every epsilon in the stated open range.

Rechecked the exact cited regular-response proof after its linked revision. Its only change treats null sites in the global conclusion. The five-rectangle body has five positive-area fibers for all allowed epsilon and no additional integer sites. Both old cap families have exactly the required regular traces and positive balance, the weight and response calculations are unchanged, and the explicit covers continue to prove global descent directly.
